NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 9 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 8 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 8, 12:23 PM ET

Brock Bowers is the top-projected tight end on the Week 9 DraftKings main slate at 17.7 DraftKings points for $7,900, at San Francisco. George Kittle (17.5, $6,000) and Trey McBride (16.3, $7,700) are next.

Greg Dulcich returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 3.36 projected points per $1,000 at $3,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 8, 12:23 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 9

Brock Bowers, LV at SF ($7,900)

Brock Bowers carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 17.7 DraftKings points at $7,900. That is 0.1 points clear of George Kittle. The model gives him 8.6 targets on 32.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.24 projected points per $1,000, 14th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 17.5 points with a simulated floor of 4.1 and a ceiling of 44.7, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 9.5-point underdog on the road against San Francisco, with an implied team total of 21 in a game totaled at 51.5.

George Kittle, SF vs LV ($6,000)

George Kittle projects 2nd at the position with 17.5 DraftKings points at $6,000. The model gives him 6.5 targets on 22.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.92 projected points per $1,000, 3rd of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Kittle averaged 17.6 points with a simulated floor of 4.0 and a ceiling of 44.8, and he holds 23% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 9.5-point favorite at home against Las Vegas, with an implied team total of 30.5 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Value: Greg Dulcich, MIA vs DET ($3,100)

Greg Dulcich projects for 10.4 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 3.36 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 21 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.1 targets on 17.5 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Dulcich averaged 10.4 points with a simulated floor of 0.1 and a ceiling of 33.7, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 6.5-point underdog at home against Detroit, with an implied team total of 21.5 in a game totaled at 49.5.
